حَرٌّ Heat; contr. of بَرْدٌ; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ حَرَارَةٌ , (S, * Msb, * K,) contr. of بُرُودَةٌ; (S;) and ↓ حُرُورٌ (S, * Msb, * K) and ↓ حِرَّةٌ : (TA:) [see 1, first sentence:] pl. [of the first] حُرُورٌ and ↓ أَحَارِرُ ; (K;) the latter anomalous, both as to its measure and in the non-incorporation of the first ر into the second: it is mentioned on the authority of AZ and others; but IDrd doubts its correctness; and the author of the Wá'ee mentions أَحَارُّ as a pl. form, but apparently to avoid contrariety to rule: the pl. of ↓ حَرَارَةٌ as a simple subst., or as an inf. n., but more probably as the former, is حَرَارَاتٌ. (TA.) ―
-b2- (assumed tropical:) A burning of the heart, from pain and wrath and distress or affliction or trouble or fatigue. (TA.) [See also حَرَارَةٌ.] ―
-b3- (assumed tropical:) Difficulty, or severity, of work. (TA.) ＝
-A2- See also حَارٌّ: ＝
-A3- and حَرَّةٌ: ＝
-A4- and سَاقُ حُرٍّ, voce حُرٌّ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
